title: High-throughput assessment of changes in the Caenorhabditis elegans gut microbiome
author: Fan Zhang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rtzd6p6
materials: Use a plotting software (Microsoft Excel, R or otherwise), to visualize growth curves by plotting OD 600 reading vs time for each well on a single chart. Verify that the growth patterns are consistent between replicates and growth curves are ordered by the dilution factor.
In a ThermoCycler run a program as follow: 01:00:00, step at 60 °C 00:15:00, step at 95 °C to desactivate the proteinase K keep on hold at 4 °C

steps.title: Transfer and initial wash
steps.instruction: Move worms from bacterial lawns into a sterilized 2 mL 96‑well deep plate and wash with M9 + 0.01 % Triton X (1000 µL for 12‑well source, 600 µL for 24‑well source); then add M9 + 0.01 % Triton X with a multichannel pipette to bring each well to a total volume of 1.8 mL.

steps.title: Five‑cycle wash to remove bacteria
steps.instruction: Perform five successive wash cycles: centrifuge the deep‑well plate at 300 g for 1 min, aspirate the supernatant using a V&P Scientific aspirating manifold (or allow worms to settle by gravity), and add fresh M9 + 0.01 % Triton X to restore the volume to 1.8 mL.

steps.title: Reduce volume to 100 µL
steps.instruction: Using the aspirating manifold, remove liquid from each well until only 100 µL remains.

steps.title: Paralyze worms with levamisole
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 10 mM levamisole in 1× M9 + 0.01 % Triton X to each well, incubate for 5 min, and confirm paralysis by microscopy before proceeding.

steps.title: Bleach treatment
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 4 % bleach solution (2 : 1 bleach : 5 M NaOH) in M9 to each well and incubate for 2 min.

steps.title: Remove bleach and levamisole
steps.instruction: Repeat the wash‑centrifuge‑aspirate cycle twice using 1× M9 + 0.01 % Triton X to eliminate residual bleach and levamisole.

steps.title: Collect supernatant control
steps.instruction: Save 100 µL of the supernatant from the final wash as a background bacterial control.

steps.title: Prepare lysate dilution for imaging
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 1× M9 + 0.01 % Triton X to each well (bringing total volume to 1 mL), mix, and transfer 100 µL of this mixture to a flat‑bottom 96‑well plate (Costar 3370).

steps.title: Capture bright‑field images
steps.instruction: Take bright‑field images of each well for later analysis of worm number, life stage, and length.

steps.title: Add garnet beads and bead‑beat
steps.instruction: Aspirate remaining liquid to 300 µL, add 1.0 mm sterilized garnet beads (Biospect) to cover the well bottom, seal with a sterile plastic mat, and bead‑beat in a Mixer Mill (Restch) or TissueLyser at 25 Hz for 5 min.

steps.title: Dilute lysate for OD assay
steps.instruction: Mix lysate by pipetting, then transfer 20 µL of lysate to a new 96‑well plate containing 180 µL 1× PBS (1 : 10 dilution).

steps.title: Set up liquid OD growth assay
steps.instruction: Transfer 20 µL of the 1 : 10 lysate dilution to a flat‑bottom 96‑well plate containing 180 µL LB per well.

steps.title: Centrifuge and reduce volume
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the deep‑well plate at 4000 g for 10 min, then remove supernatant to leave 190 µL of liquid.

steps.title: Freeze lysate overnight
steps.instruction: Seal the plate and store at –80 °C overnight.

steps.title: Second bead‑beat for bacterial lysis
steps.instruction: Thaw the plate, add 0.1 mm sterile zirconia/silica beads (BioSpec) to cover the well bottom, and bead‑beat in a Mixer Mill or TissueLyser for 5 min.

steps.title: Prepare serial dilutions for CFU counting
steps.instruction: Fill a flat‑bottom 96‑well plate with 180 µL sterile filtered PBS per well; add 20 µL of the microbiome mixture to four replicate wells in column 1 (A1‑D1) and 20 µL LB to the remaining wells of column 1 as controls; then perform a 1 : 10 serial dilution across columns 2‑12 using a multichannel pipette, changing tips between columns.

steps.title: Plate dilutions on agar
steps.instruction: Spot 10 µL of each dilution onto rectangular LB agar plates with a multichannel pipette, incubate overnight at the optimal temperature, and count colonies where possible.

steps.title: Set up growth plate for OD monitoring
steps.instruction: Fill each well of a flat‑bottom 96‑well plate with 180 µL LB, transfer 20 µL from each dilution well (step 16) to the corresponding LB well, incubate at the optimal temperature with intermittent shaking, and measure OD₆₀₀ every 15‑30 min until growth is observed in all wells.

steps.title: Determine linear OD range and threshold
steps.instruction: Identify the OD₆₀₀ linear range of each growth curve and calculate Threshold = ((ODmax – ODmin)/2) + ODmin.

steps.title: Calculate slope and intercept
steps.instruction: Using only OD₆₀₀ data points within the linear range, compute the slope and intercept for each well.

steps.title: Compute time to reach threshold
steps.instruction: For each well, calculate Time = (Threshold – Intercept) / Slope.

steps.title: Convert threshold time to CFU
steps.instruction: Plot CFU values (from step 17) versus threshold times, fit an exponential trendline, obtain R² and the equation, and use this equation to convert threshold times of samples to CFU.

steps.title: Calculate CFU per animal
steps.instruction: Compute CFU / animal = (CFU × dilution factor) / number of animals for each sample.

steps.title: Add proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of 20 mg/mL proteinase K to each well.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect DNA template
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate for 10 min at 4000 g, transfer 100 µL supernatant to a clean 96‑well PCR plate (keep at 4 °C short‑term or –80 °C long‑term); use filter tips and avoid contaminating the tip groove.

steps.title: Prepare 2× Taq master mix
steps.instruction: In a 5 mL tube combine 1.25 mL 2× Taq Master Mix, 100 µL 515F primer, and 1 mL H₂O (total 2.35 mL).

steps.title: Dispense master mix
steps.instruction: Add 23 µL of the freshly mixed master mix to each well of a new 96‑well PCR plate.

steps.title: Add reverse primer
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL of 806R reverse primer to each PCR well.

steps.title: Add DNA template
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL of the supernatant (step 23) as DNA template to each PCR well; store remaining supernatant at –80 °C.

steps.title: Run PCR
steps.instruction: Place the PCR plate in a thermocycler and run the appropriate 16S rRNA amplification program.

steps.title: Verify PCR on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1.5 % agarose gel, mix 2 µL loading dye with 4 µL PCR product per sample, load 5 µL plus a 1 kb ladder, and run the gel.

steps.title: Purify PCR product
steps.instruction: Purify the amplified product using a commercial PCR purification kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Quantify and pool libraries
steps.instruction: Quantify band intensity (gel or fluorometry), normalize each library by volume, and pool equal amounts of all libraries into a single tube.

steps.title: Submit for multiplex sequencing
steps.instruction: Submit the pooled library for multiplex sequencing together with the appropriate sequencing primer.
